identity.title: Pulmonary crackles: bibasilar (heart failure) vs focal/unilateral (pneumonia)

technique.how: With the patient sitting, auscultate posterior bases and all fields during slow deep breaths through an open mouth, comparing sides. Have the patient cough before calling crackles persistent; note timing (late-inspiratory fine = edema/fibrosis; coarse = secretions), distribution (bibasilar symmetric vs focal), and whether they clear with position change.
technique.prerequisites: Quiet room, diaphragm on skin, patient able to take deep breaths; re-listen after several deep breaths because dependent atelectasis crackles clear.

interpretation.positive_finding: Bibasilar symmetric late-inspiratory crackles in an acutely dyspneic adult raise the probability of heart failure (pooled specificity ~0.77-0.81); focal/unilateral crackles with fever or cough raise the probability of pneumonia (pooled LR+ ~2.4). Crackles are non-specific and also occur in ILD, atelectasis, COPD and bronchiectasis.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of crackles lowers the probability of heart failure only moderately (LR- 0.35-0.51) and does not exclude pneumonia; normal vital signs plus a normal lung examination together make CAP unlikely (LR- 0.10).
interpretation.pitfalls: Dependent-atelectasis crackles clear with deep breaths or cough; chronic 'velcro' crackles of fibrosis mimic edema; in chronic HF crackles are often absent despite high wedge pressure, and obese or shallow-breathing patients give false negatives.
interpretation.changes_what: Bibasilar crackles favor HF (add JVP, S3, BNP/POCUS); focal crackles with fever favor pneumonia (CXR); clear lungs do not rule out either but lower HF probability modestly.

estimates.target_condition: Congestive heart failure as cause of dyspnea (absence of rales)
estimates.population: Adult ED patients presenting with dyspnea; RCE pooled analysis
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical/echo-based HF diagnosis per included studies

estimates.target_condition: Heart failure as cause of acute dyspnea (lung crepitations/rales)
estimates.population: Adults with a new episode of acute dyspnea; 8 ED studies, 4737 patients; HF prevalence 25-59%
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis of HF per included studies
estimates.quote: NLR was between 0.59 and 1.29 with one outlier: rales (pooled NLR=0.35)
estimates.location: Abstract, Results (specificity 0.77 in Abstract, Conclusion: 'lung crepitations (0.77, pooled odds ratio: 11)')

estimates.target_condition: Heart failure (new diagnosis) in primary care (lung crepitations)
estimates.population: Patients with suspected heart failure in primary care; IPD meta-analysis of 9 studies
estimates.reference_standard: Echocardiography / expert panel per included studies
estimates.quote: orthopnoea (89%), oedema (72%), elevated jugular venous pressure (70%), cardiomegaly (85%), added heart sounds (99%), lung crepitations (81%)

estimates.population: Adults >=18 without serious illness or immunosuppression presenting to primary care/outpatient/emergency clinics with respiratory symptoms; 13 studies, 11,144 participants; pneumonia prevalence 5-50%

estimates.target_condition: Community-acquired pneumonia; COMPOSITE rule-out = normal vital signs AND normal pulmonary examination (no crackles or other auscultatory abnormality)
estimates.population: Outpatient adults/adolescents with acute respiratory infection; 3 studies; baseline CAP risk ~4%
estimates.quote: had a summary estimate of LR- of 0.10 (95% CI, 0.07 to 0.13) with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.92

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use clear lungs to exclude heart failure in chronic HF patients (crackles are often absent with high filling pressures) or to exclude pneumonia in the elderly/immunocompromised, where auscultation is insensitive.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Diffuse crackles with hypoxemia and hypotension suggest pulmonary edema from cardiogenic shock or ARDS and require immediate escalation regardless of etiology.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Agreement on crackles is only fair to moderate between examiners (Metlay RCE); distribution and persistence after cough are more reliable than presence alone.

extraction_notes: Wang 2005 table LR+ for rales (~2.8) is not visible in the abstract; only the abstract LR- 0.51 is entered. The Eur J Emerg Med 2018 pooled NLR 0.35 and specificity 0.77 come from different abstract sentences; sensitivity is given only as a range (0.32-0.88) and left null. Htun 2019 PMC full text is truncated by the tool at ~20 kB so its results table could not be read; the abstract LR+ (2.42) is used. Marchello 2019 LR- 0.10 is a composite (normal vitals plus normal lung exam), clearly labeled, not crackles alone. Metlay 1997 and Ebell 2020 abstracts carry no crackles-specific numbers; cited for context (Ebell reports egophony LR+ 6.17 and dullness 2.62, which belong to other records). No abstract-level estimate found for focal vs bibasilar distribution.
